template.title: 5 Tips to Avoid Fibrosis After Your Lipo
template.author: By: Guitar Curves Team
template.intro: Fibrosis is not "bad luck", it's a lack of proper compression. Here we explain how to use your ab board correctly to sculpt perfect results.

tips.title: 1. Constant pressure is key
tips.desc: Imagine your skin is "floating" above the muscle after surgery. If empty space remains, the body fills it with disorganized scar tissue (fibrosis). The secret is not to squeeze until you suffocate, but to maintain uniform and flat pressure.

tips.title: 2. Hydration with Vitamin E
tips.desc: Traumatized skin needs nutrition. Our fajas' high compression fabric is no ordinary cloth; it is infused with microcapsules of Vitamin E, Ginkgo Biloba, and Seaweed. Upon contact with your body heat, these capsules break and release nutrients directly into your skin while you wear it.

tips.title: 3. Stage 2 is crucial
tips.desc: Many patients make the mistake of staying with the post-surgical faja (Stage 1) for 3 months. Error! At 2-3 weeks, when inflammation goes down, that faja will be too big. You need to move to a High Compression Faja (Stage 2) to continue sculpting the waist. If the faja doesn't squeeze you, it's not working.

tips.title: 4. Use Foam (Lipo Foam)
tips.desc: The board is rigid, but the foam is soft. Use foam under the board to protect your skin from marks and ensure compression reaches every corner.

tips.title: 5. Lymphatic Drainage
tips.desc: Don't skip your massages. They help remove retained fluid that the faja is mobilizing.

template.quote: "70% of a lipo result depends on post-operative care, not the surgery itself." — Dr. Plastic Surgeon

faqs.question: How do I know my correct size?
faqs.answer: Our fajas are medical grade and have very high compression. We recommend using our 'Guitar Ratio' calculator or the size chart. If you're between two sizes, always choose the larger one for initial comfort.

faqs.question: Can I wear this garment daily?
faqs.answer: Yes, most of our Sculpt collection is designed to be invisible under daily clothing. Recovery Stage 2 garments can also be worn daily once your doctor authorizes it (usually after week 6).

faqs.question: Do you ship internationally?
faqs.answer: Yes, we ship worldwide from our main distribution center. Shipping times vary between 3-7 business days depending on your location.

faqs.question: What is your exchange policy?
faqs.answer: We offer a 'Perfect Fit' satisfaction guarantee. If your faja doesn't fit, you have 30 days to exchange it for another size, as long as the garment is in its original packaging and unused (for hygiene).

faqs.question: Why do I need a special bra after my surgery?
faqs.answer: After a mammoplasty or lift, your tissues need constant support to prevent sagging while they heal. Our medical-grade bras provide the exact compression to reduce inflammation, prevent fluid retention, and ensure your implants settle in the correct position.

faqs.question: How long should I wear the post-surgical bra?
faqs.answer: Most surgeons recommend continuous wear (24/7) for the first 6 weeks. After this period, you can switch to wearing it during the day or night per medical recommendation. Our designs are so comfortable that many clients continue using them as daily bras for the back support they offer.

faqs.question: How does it help with posture?
faqs.answer: The weight of implants can cause back pain and hunched shoulders. Our bras feature an 'X' reinforcement or high back support that gently forces you to keep your shoulders back and spine aligned, relieving tension immediately.

faqs.question: Do the bras have underwires?
faqs.answer: No. During recovery, underwires (metal hoops) are prohibited because they can hurt incisions or alter the shape of the implant. Our 'Wireless Support' technology lifts and supports the bust using smart cuts in high compression fabric, without the need for uncomfortable metals.

faqs.question: WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN STAGE 1 AND STAGE 2 FAJAS?
faqs.answer: Stage 1 is low compression for the first 7-10 days of swelling. Stage 2 (our specialty) is high compression and is mandatory from week 2 to sculpt the figure and adhere the skin.

faqs.question: HOW DO I KNOW MY SIZE IF MY WAIST IS SWOLLEN?
faqs.answer: Don't buy your pants size. Measure your current waist and hips. If you're between two sizes in Stage 2, choose the larger one or use extenders. Visit our Size Guide.

faqs.question: WHY DO I NEED A PERINEAL OPENING OR ZIPPER?
faqs.answer: The first days of recovery are difficult. Our perineal closure and bottom zipper system is designed to allow you to go to the bathroom without having to remove the entire faja, which would be painful and complicated.

faqs.question: HOW TO AVOID FIBROSIS?
faqs.answer: Constant use of a high compression faja (Stage 2) helps maintain uniform pressure on the skin, preventing irregular fluid accumulation that causes fibrosis.

items.question: Why do I need a special bra after my surgery?
items.answer: After a mammoplasty or lift, your tissues need constant support to prevent sagging while they heal. Our medical-grade bras provide the exact compression to reduce inflammation, avoid fluid retention, and ensure your implants settle in the correct position.

items.question: How long should I wear the post-surgical bra?
items.answer: Most surgeons recommend continuous use (24/7) for the first 6 weeks. After this period, you can switch to wearing it during the day or night according to medical advice. Our designs are so comfortable that many clients continue to wear them as a daily bra for the back support they offer.

items.question: How does it help with posture?
items.answer: The weight of implants can cause back pain and hunched shoulders. Our bras feature an 'X' reinforcement or high back support that gently forces you to keep your shoulders back and spine aligned, relieving tension immediately.

items.question: Do the bras have underwires?
items.answer: No. During recovery, underwires (metal rings) are forbidden because they can hurt incisions or alter the implant shape. Our 'Wireless Support' technology lifts and holds the bust using intelligent cuts in high-compression fabric, without need for uncomfortable metals.

items.question: How do I know if I need a Stage 1 or Stage 2 Faja?
items.answer: Stage 1 is low compression, ideal for the first post-op week when you are very swollen. Stage 2 (our specialty) is high compression and is used starting from week 2 or 3 to mold and adhere skin to muscle.

items.question: Does the Guitar Curves model work if I haven't had surgery?
items.answer: Yes! If your body is natural but you have a small waist and wide hips, our fajas will prevent back rolls or digging into your thighs too much.

items.question: How do I go to the bathroom with the faja on?
items.answer: All our Stage 2 and 3 fajas feature a perineal zipper or an anatomical opening designed so you don't have to take it off every time you go to the bathroom.

items.question: If I am S in waist but XL in hips, what size do I order?
items.answer: This is Guitar Curves' specialty. Our 'Guitar' size is designed specifically for this proportion. If you select a regular size, it will be loose at the waist. In our Size Guide check for 'Guitar' or 'BBL' options which have a 2-size difference between waist and hip.

items.question: When will my order ship?
items.answer: Orders placed before 2:00 PM EST ship the same day. Standard shipping takes 3-5 business days within the USA. We offer Express options if you need it urgent for your surgery.

returns_policy.title: Exchange Policy
returns_policy.subtitle: We designed the following policies to provide a quick and simple solution in case you need to make an exchange
returns_policy.recommendations_desc: It is important to follow the following recommendations when trying on your faja so that your purchase is not damaged and remains eligible for return or exchange.
recommendations_list: Wear underwear, keep your body free of body lotions, deodorants, oils, powders, perfumes, makeup, or beauty products that could transfer to the garment.
Avoid pulling the garment from thin areas like the glute area and silicone lace.
Do not use jewelry, be careful with long nails or any sharp instruments that help close or adjust the garment.
If you are in the post-surgical or postpartum recovery stage, remember to adequately cover any part of your body that underwent surgery to avoid stains or discoloration.

faq_accordion.title: Doubts on how to measure?
faq_accordion.intro: How to measure correctly: Forget your pant size. Colombian fajas are engineering garments and require exact measurements.
faq_accordion.waist_text: Place the tape measure just above your belly button (narrowest part of torso).
faq_accordion.waist_tip: Pro Tip: Tighten tape slightly, just how you'd like the faja to hug you.
faq_accordion.hip_text: Feet together, pass tape around the fullest part of your glutes.
faq_accordion.note: If your measurements put you between sizes, always choose the larger one (especially if you are Stage 1 or swollen).
